advanced/context-propagation.title: Context Propagation
advanced/context-propagation.description: Understanding how TraceChain propagates runid and stepid through your code helps you write correct, observable workflows — especially in async or multi-threaded environments.

advanced/custom-clients.title: Custom Clients
advanced/custom-clients.description: By default, every TraceChain decorator uses a singleton client configured from environment variables. You can override this with a custom TraceChainClient for more control.

advanced/prompt-versioning.title: Prompt Versioning
advanced/prompt-versioning.description: TraceChain includes a prompt registry — a versioned store of prompt templates. Link each @llm_step to a stored version and see per-version quality metrics in the dashboard.

backend/api-reference.title: API Reference
backend/api-reference.description: All endpoints return JSON. Error responses follow the FastAPI default shape "message"}.

backend/database.title: Database Schema
backend/database.description: TraceChain uses PostgreSQL with five tables. All primary keys are UUID strings.

backend/overview.title: Backend Overview
backend/overview.description: The TraceChain backend is a FastAPI application that stores all observability data in PostgreSQL. It is the central storage and query layer between the SDK and the dashboard.

dashboard/overview.title: Dashboard Overview
dashboard/overview.description: The TraceChain dashboard is a Next.js 14 application (App Router, Tailwind CSS, Recharts) that gives you a visual interface over all your workflow observability data.

deployment/docker.title: Docker Deployment
deployment/docker.description: TraceChain ships a docker-compose.yml that starts the entire stack with one command.

deployment/environment-variables.title: Environment Variables
deployment/environment-variables.description: Complete reference for all environment variables across all three TraceChain components.

getting-started/configuration.title: Configuration
getting-started/configuration.description: All TraceChain configuration is read from environment variables (with .env file support via python-dotenv).

getting-started/installation.title: Installation
getting-started/installation.description: TraceChain has three components. You need all three for a complete setup, but you can instrument your code with the SDK before the backend is running.

getting-started/quickstart.title: Quickstart
getting-started/quickstart.description: This guide takes you from zero to a fully traced LLM workflow. By the end you will see your first run in the dashboard.

intro.title: What is TraceChain?
intro.description: TraceChain is a reliability-first observability framework for LLM workflows. It gives you full visibility into every step, every LLM call, every token spent, and every failure — without changing how you write your pipeline logic.

sdk/evaluations.title: Evaluations
sdk/evaluations.description: TraceChain can automatically score the quality of each run. Scores are stored in the database and displayed on the run detail page.

sdk/llm-step.title: @llm_step
sdk/llm-step.description: The @llm_step decorator wraps a function that makes a single LLM API call. It records the prompt, response, token counts, estimated cost, and latency — and accumulates cost/tokens toward the run total.

sdk/overview.title: SDK Overview
sdk/overview.description: The TraceChain SDK is a zero-friction instrumentation library for Python. It uses decorators and context variables so you add observability by annotating functions — not by threading IDs through every call.

sdk/replay.title: Replay
sdk/replay.description: Replay lets you re-execute a previous workflow run with the same input. The new run is linked to the original so you can compare outputs, costs, and quality scores side by side.

sdk/step.title: @step
sdk/step.description: The @step decorator instruments a discrete unit of work inside a workflow. It records timing, input, output, errors, and optionally retries on failure.

sdk/tracing.title: Tracing Context
sdk/tracing.description: TraceChain propagates runid and stepid through Python's contextvars module. You rarely need to interact with these directly, but they are useful for custom logging, manual backend calls, or advanced integrations.

sdk/workflow.title: @workflow
sdk/workflow.description: The @workflow decorator is the entry point for TraceChain instrumentation. It wraps your pipeline function and manages the full lifecycle of a workflow run record.
